stem: A postoperative client has an order for intermittent pneumatic sequential compression devices on the legs. What complication is this intervention intended to help prevent?
rationale: AHRQ identifies intermittent pneumatic compression devices as a form of mechanical venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis used in surgical patients, including when anticoagulant prophylaxis is contraindicated or as part of combined prophylaxis in higher-risk patients. Their purpose is to reduce venous stasis and help prevent DVT/VTE.
educational_objective: Recognize intermittent pneumatic compression as mechanical VTE prophylaxis used to help prevent postoperative DVT.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Preventing Hospital-Associated Venous Thromboembolism: A Guide for Effective Quality Improvement
source_locator: Chapter 3 > Intermittent Pneumatic Compression Devices; Appendix A > mechanical prophylaxis and DVT prophylaxis
source_claim_supported: Intermittent pneumatic compression devices are mechanical prophylaxis used in surgical patients to prevent DVT/VTE, either alone in selected circumstances or with pharmacologic prophylaxis.
correction_summary: Replaced the nonprimary ACCP attribution with an accessible AHRQ VTE-prevention source and removed explanatory cueing from all distractors while preserving the correct prophylactic purpose.
audit_findings: A is the direct purpose of IPC/SCD mechanical prophylaxis. B, C, and D are not prevented by the device's venous-compression mechanism. No second answer remains.
